$comment: This file is the declarative source of truth for what the demo asserts. It is
read by demo/seed.ts and demo/run.ts so the presenter checklist and the seeding
Every source-chain transaction referenced here is REAL, staged by us on Ethereum
Sepolia using canonical WETH — a token we do not control. Clearbook deploys
nothing on the source chain. These addresses are throwaway demo wallets and
describe no real borrower, lender, or agreement.
expectedError values are the contract's own custom error names. They are
assertions, not documentation: seed.ts fails if the chain disagrees.

covenant.statement: No repayment may come from an address this originator's own treasury funded for at least the repayment amount, in the same token, within W source-chain blocks.

economics.note: A successful challenge slashes the full per-loan bond; half goes to the challenger, half to the protocol sink (the burn address).

why: The borrower repaid from funds this treasury did not supply for that purpose.
Citing the loan's own disbursement as the funding leg is refused by condition 11,
which exists precisely so an honest loan cannot be made to look circular.
Nobody had to trust us for this outcome — the contract refuses on its own.
The treasury funded the payer, then the payer repaid the treasury, inside the
window the originator itself published and bonded against.
All eleven conditions hold, so challenge() slashes the bond in one transaction.
This is the leg the judge performs live from their own wallet.
Citing a verified transfer that has nothing to do with this loan's payer is
refused by condition 5. Verified evidence is not the same as relevant evidence.
Shown as a pre-flight red X in the challenge console before any gas is spent.
Disbursement only, with maturityBlock passed and no repayment claimed.
Anyone may call markDelinquent() — no privileged role is involved.
Not staged by default: it costs a fourth loan's bond and adds nothing the
breach path does not already prove. Enable with seed.ts --with-delinquent.

invariants: I1 · the contract's balance always covers the sum of posted bonds
I2 · every originator's bond is at least its exposure
I3 · a verified fact backs at most one claim
I5 · no fact whose source receipt reverted is ever stored
